blast_radius: Writes category/escalation flags onto tickets; drives routing, not sending.

throughput.derivation: Read-only database query inside the service's own container over one SSH session. count by day(classified_at) over a trailing window; 24h = classified_at >= now()-24h.
notes: 30-day category mix (illustrative): other 700, refund 500, escalated 300, cancellation 200, dispute 100, fraud 50.
A minority of tickets classified in 24h are flagged for escalation (illustrative: 20 of 100).
throughput.signal_path: postgres://example-service-db/example_service (container-local; credentials in EXAMPLE_SERVICE_* env, never read by capmap)#tickets.classified_at

verification.note: Graded on throughput, not liveness: a running loop with zero volume is DEGRADED.
verification.source: postgres://example-service-db/example_service (container-local; credentials in EXAMPLE_SERVICE_* env, never read by capmap)#tickets.classified_at

what_it_does: Ticket classifier for the support pipeline; volume is tickets stamped with a classification timestamp in the window.
why_it_matters: Classification is the step that decides how a ticket is routed (refund / dispute / fraud / escalate); a stalled classifier means every downstream routing decision goes stale.
